subject: economics
title: Kinked Demand and Price Wars
welcome_lead: Sweezy's kinked demand explains why oligopoly prices are sticky.
meta_desc: A-Level Oligopoly: kinked demand curve and price competition.
final_note: Sticky prices and non-price competition mark oligopoly markets.

concepts.def: Demand curve with a kink at the prevailing price.
Dominant firm setting price followed by rivals.
Mutual price cutting that destroys margins.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sweezy's kinked demand assumes rivals will match price cuts (so demand is inelastic below the kink) but ignore price rises (elastic above). Result: prices are sticky.
Price wars erupt when one firm tries to grab share. They destroy margins and rarely shift share permanently - supermarket bread wars cost millions and changed little.
Overt cartels like OPEC formally fix output; most are illegal under competition law. Tacit collusion (silent following of a leader) avoids prosecution but reaches similar outcomes.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: Demand always falls when supply increases.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
A change in price shifts the demand curve.

mcqs.q: What is the predicted effect of a binding price ceiling like rent control?
options: Price ceilings only affect the rich.
Price ceilings make goods cheaper for everyone with no downsides.
Shortage in the market — quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the controlled price, leading to queues, black markets and reduced quality.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
